chunk_text: Within a Text-to-SQL pipeline, MDL serves both as a semantic grounding mechanism for LLMs and as an operational layer that deterministically rewrites semantic queries into executable, dialect-specific SQL. Methodologically, Wren’s semantic layer follows a structured, engineering-driven workflow. First, MDL artifacts are authored or generated from existing enterprise metadata sources, including database schemas, documentation, and example queries; these artifacts define logical models, attributes, join relationships, and metric formulas. Second, the Wren Engine builds a runtime semantic index and query compiler. When a natural language question is issued, the engine resolves business terms to MDL entities, expands metric definitions into canonical SQL expressions, enforces approved join paths and accesscontrol policies, and finally transpiles the logical query into backend-specific SQL (for example, for BigQuery, PostgreSQL, or Snowflake).
